# CreateHtmlView 〔BlitzLLVM〕

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzPlus](BlitzPlus) · [Gadgets](BlitzPlus-Gadgets)

</div>


```blitzbasic
CreateHtmlView:Int32 x:Int32, y:Int32, width:Int32, height:Int32, group:Int32, style:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | Int32 | required | Horizontal position inside the group. |
| `y` | Int32 | required | Vertical position inside the group. |
| `width` | Int32 | required | Width of the gadget. |
| `height` | Int32 | required | Height of the gadget. |
| `group` | Int32 | required | The window or group the gadget is in. |
| `style` | Int32 | `0` | 0 nothing, 1 no context menu, 2 do not follow links. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns:** The handle of the gadget.

## Description

**〔BlitzLLVM〕** This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Makes a gadget that is meant to show a web page, and returns its handle. The style 1 stops the context menu and 2 stops the user from following links (the link is then given by [HtmlViewEventURL](HtmlViewEventURL)); both are accepted and ignored.

## Differences

* There is no web browser inside the window yet: the gadget is a frame that shows the address it was sent to, and no page is loaded. Windows could embed WebView for it; Linux and macOS have nothing similar. The original BlitzPlus had this command turned off in its runtime too.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
win = CreateWindow("Browser", 10, 10, 300, 200, Desktop(), 3)
html = CreateHtmlView(0, 0, 290, 160, win)
SetGadgetLayout html, 1, 1, 1, 1
HtmlViewGo html, "https://www.blitzbasic.com"
Repeat
Until WaitEvent() = $803
```
